open_points.subject: Overall progress denominator when a planned-work section has no SectionProgress
open_points.text: “overall progress (weighted by `work_planned` across sections with planned work)” conflicts with “a section without a progress record is left out of the sum, as it is left out of overall progress”
open_points.question: Does the overall-progress denominator include every active-budget section with planned work, or only those having a progress record?
options: Include every section with planned work; absence makes its contribution unavailable rather than removing its planned weight.
Exclude sections without progress records from both numerator and denominator.
open_points.default_guess: Follow the newer A9-specific sentence and exclude sections without progress records.

witness.initial: An active budget has section A with work_planned 100 and section B with work_planned 100; neither initially has a SectionProgress record.
events: A staff member records completion_percent 100 for section A.
outcomes: Weighting across all sections with planned work yields 50% overall progress.
Leaving section B out of overall progress yields 100% overall progress.
witness.observer: The viewer reading the project's progress.

open_points.subject: PaymentSummaryView completed-work total and work balance after nullable section values
open_points.text: “`completed_work_total` (here and in `BudgetView`) is the sum of the sections' `completed_work_value` that are not `None`” does not say whether the same rule applies to `PaymentSummaryView.completed_work_total`, although that projection also uses the total to produce `work_balance`.
open_points.question: When one or more planned sections lack progress records, does PaymentSummaryView sum only recorded completed-work values and compute a balance, or is its completed-work total and therefore the payment component unavailable?
options: Apply the same non-`None` summation rule to PaymentSummaryView and compute work_balance from that partial total.
Treat completed work as unavailable when required section progress is absent, so PaymentSummaryView cannot be returned as available.
Give PaymentSummaryView a distinct completed-work-total rule explicitly defined for missing SectionProgress records.
open_points.default_guess: Apply the same non-`None` summation rule to PaymentSummaryView for consistency with ProgressView and BudgetView.

witness.initial: An active budget has two planned-work sections; section A has recorded completed_work_value 100, section B has no SectionProgress record, and the project has payments totaling 60.
events: A viewer requests the project overview, including payments.
outcomes: The payment component is available with completed_work_total 100 and work_balance 40.
The payment component is unavailable because the completed-work total needed for its balance is incomplete.
witness.observer: The viewer reading the payment summary and work-balance label.
